lastText: File ClosedA Republic Remembered by MarzabottoMajor DefeatItalian High Command, 1939–1945End of hostilities: APRIL 28, 1945 · filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathThe Italian Social Republic ends on April 28, 1945, twenty months after Mussolini's rescue from Gran Sasso █████████ it as a German client state in the occupied north. The human cost of this path runs ██████ than the historical one at nearly every hinge point: Italy's own ███████ dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the ██████ tolls of any Axis power relative to population. War was declared on Britain alone, ██████ after France had already settled its own armistice without Italian participation: a different opening than the historical one, fought for the Mediterranean prize directly rather than for a seat at a peace table that no longer existed to claim. Graziani ordered the withdrawal from the fortified camps before Compass's flanking attack landed, ██████ than holding as the historical delay did: sparing the Tenth Army the worst of a rout that historically cost some 130,000 men taken prisoner. Malta was taken in an actual 1940 invasion, while the garrison was still weak, then lost back to a determined British counter-effort over the following winter, the documented British commitment to the island reasserting itself even against an early and successful Italian gamble.
